pixels/label: A classifier gives a whole image one label. Segmentation labels every pixel: this one is sky, that one tree, those ground.
pixels/shrink: A ConvNet shrinks as it goes. Strided convolutions and pooling take a sixty four by sixty four image down to eight by eight, with two hundred and fifty six channels.
pixels/grow: To label every pixel, it must grow back: one score per class at every pixel, C by sixty four by sixty four. Each pixel's highest score is its label.
stamp/setup: The layer that grows is a transposed convolution. Here is an input of three numbers, one, two and three, and a filter, w: one, two, one.
stamp/first: Each input value stamps a copy of the filter, scaled by that value, into the output. The one stamps one, two, one.
stamp/next: The next stamp lands S further along: two places, with a stride of two. The two stamps two, four, two.
stamp/add: Where stamps overlap, they add. Position two gets one plus two: three.
stamp/all: The three stamps three, six, three. Add it all up: one, two, three, four, five, six, three. Three numbers became seven.
size/starts: How long is the output? The first stamp starts at zero, and each of the other W minus one starts S further on. So the last starts at S times W minus one: four.
size/width: Add the last stamp's width, F, and the output is seven long.
size/pad: Padding works backwards here: it trims P entries off each end. With P of one, seven becomes five. So the size is S times W minus one, plus F, minus two P.
size/undo: It is the convolution size rule, run backwards. A convolution with a filter of four, stride two and padding one takes thirty two down to sixteen. The transposed one takes sixteen back: two times fifteen, plus four, minus two, is thirty two.
